# Git Workflow

Curated by Skill Harbor: a complete Git workflow reference for teams of all sizes. Three branching strategies compared (GitHub Flow for continuous deployment, trunk-based for high-velocity teams with feature flags, GitFlow for scheduled enterprise releases) with a when-to-use table. Conventional Commits format with the type table (feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore, perf, ci, revert), good vs bad examples, and a commit message template. Merge vs rebase explained with rules (merge preserves history for shared branches, rebase for clean local history, never rebase pushed shared branches). PR workflow with title format, description template, reviewer and author checklists. Conflict resolution (identify, resolve manually or with mergetool, accept one side), plus prevention strategies. Branch naming conventions and cleanup commands, stash workflow, semantic versioning and releases with tags, changelog generation, essential git configs and aliases, gitignore patterns, undoing mistakes (reset, revert, amend), git hooks examples, anti-patterns, and a quick reference table. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: a pure knowledge reference, nothing to install; team conventions should be agreed together, not imposed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
